key_insight: In a large health check-up cohort, chest X-ray AI showed strong concordance with routine radiologist reading, especially for pulmonary nodules and masses, and sometimes flagged lung cancer earlier in retrospective review.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest AI could help support chest radiograph workflows in screening settings, but prospective studies are still needed to confirm real-world benefit.
method: Retrospective single-center analysis of 298,991 chest radiographs from 114,866 people (2019–2023).
AI was compared with routine double reading by board-certified radiologists using two predefined positivity thresholds.
A subset of 48 histopathologically confirmed lung cancers was reviewed retrospectively for AI-vs-radiologist timing.
evidence_signal: Radiologist-referenced performance was 72.0% sensitivity and 79.6% specificity for any of 10 findings, and 87.1% sensitivity and 91.8% specificity for nodule/mass detection, with negative predictive values of 99.0% and 100.0%.
watch_item: Because the reference standard was routine radiologist judgment rather than universal CT or pathology, the results reflect operational concordance and exploratory retrospective signals rather than proven clinical outcome improvement.
paper_title: Chest Radiography AI Concordance and Lung Cancer Linkage in a Large Health Check-up Cohort
